sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner - accused seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.1277 of 2025 on the file of the learned XV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally,
registered for the offences under Sections 420, 406 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").

entities.text: XV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard the submissions of Sri Kolli Ganapathi, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3.
The learned petitioner counsel has submitted that he has not cheated anyone and that the allegations do not attract the ingredients of the alleged offences.
He further argued that he has not forged any document and there is no element of truth in the allegations.
He therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings.

4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has opposed saying that the present petitioner claimed to be the real owner of the building and has collected Rs.30 Lakhs from the de facto complainant and later on has taken to one Dinesh Kumar saying that he is the owner of the building and that Rs.20 Lakhs is given to said Dinesh Kumar and the petitioner herein has taken Rs.30 Lakhs by representing that he would get the internal works done in the building to facilitate the running of hostel by the de facto complainant, for which purpose he intended to take the building.
The allegations do point out that the petitioner entertained dishonest intention from the inception of the alleged act and hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
The record reveals that there was some online transfers of money and account to account transfer alleged to have been made by the de facto complainant into the account of the petitioner herein.
The said transactions are the subject matter of trial to bring out the truth in the said transactions.
The C.C. is pending on the file of XV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally for trial.

sentences.text: Thus, in the facts and circumstances, it is deemed appropriate to dispose of the petition by dispensing with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial Court.
